subsystems.name: Pressure housing
subsystems.role: holds one atmosphere inside while the Venus surface pushes in at about 92 bar, and gives sensors a window to the outside.

subsystems.name: High-temperature electronics
subsystems.role: computes, controls and stores data at 460 °C with no cooling loop.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supplies electricity for weeks to months in an environment where solar power is negligible and batteries normally last hours.
parts: or a radioisotope heat source with a high-temperature converter

subsystems.name: Thermal design
subsystems.role: accepts that everything equilibrates to 460 °C, and manages the transient heating during descent rather than fighting the ambient.

subsystems.name: Sensors and sampling
subsystems.role: measures atmospheric composition, surface chemistry and imagery.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: sends data to an orbiter relay, since direct-to-Earth links from the surface are weak.

subsystems.name: Entry, descent and landing
subsystems.role: delivers the lander through the atmosphere to a soft landing.

buildSteps.title: Design for ambient, not for cooling
buildSteps.detail: Every component is specified to work at 460 °C. The design deliberately avoids refrigerators, coolant loops and conventional silicon chips, which would need to be kept cool.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate silicon carbide circuits
buildSteps.detail: Silicon carbide wafers are processed with high-temperature ion implantation and anneals, and metallisation that survives 500 °C. Wafers are probed and tested hot, not at room temperature.

buildSteps.title: Package and interconnect
buildSteps.detail: Dies are mounted in ceramic or metal packages with high-temperature die attach and bond wires. Polymers and solder are avoided because they fail far below Venus temperatures.

buildSteps.title: Build the pressure housing
buildSteps.detail: The shell is machined or formed, welded, and fitted with sapphire windows and metal seals. It is proof-tested to well above 92 bar before anything goes inside.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the power source
buildSteps.detail: If battery-powered, thermal or high-temperature lithium cells are stacked and insulated. If radioisotope-powered, the heat source is encapsulated and coupled to a converter designed for a 460 °C cold sink.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and bake
buildSteps.detail: Subsystems are assembled and run in a Venus simulation chamber at about 460 °C and 92 bar in carbon dioxide, measuring drift and lifetime over hundreds of hours.

buildSteps.title: Qualify for launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: Vibration, shock and thermal-vacuum testing reproduce launch and the cold cruise to Venus.

buildSteps.title: Land and operate
buildSteps.detail: After aeroshell entry and parachute descent, the lander touches down, releases covers, deploys sensors and begins transmitting through a relay orbiter.

prerequisites.why: discrete transistors and simple circuits have been demonstrated at 500 °C in laboratories, but complex processors and memory are not yet available.
every join, seal and package must survive 460 °C for months without polymers or ordinary solder.
primary batteries give hours, and a radioisotope converter has a very hot cold sink, making it inefficient and unproven at Venus conditions.
spectrometers and gas sensors have been tested hot, but long-lived calibrated instruments are immature.
chambers such as NASA Glenn's Venus simulation rig reproduce 460 °C and 92 bar with carbon dioxide for ground testing.
Soviet Venera landers proved parachute descent and soft landing from 1970 onward, though only for roughly two hours of surface life.

pathway.milestone: silicon carbide devices and sensors survive extended lab tests at 460 °C
pathway.unlocks: confidence that a lander can operate without cooling.

pathway.milestone: a small short-lived lander using silicon carbide electronics and primary batteries
pathway.unlocks: flight proof of packaging, seals and hot electronics, lasting hours to days.

pathway.milestone: a radioisotope-powered lander lasting weeks to months
pathway.unlocks: the first genuinely long-duration Venus surface mission.

pathway.milestone: a surface station or network with seismology and long-term chemistry
pathway.unlocks: sustained Venus surface science rather than brief snapshots.
